pk.context: 10 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

pill.desc: white, round, bi-convex, film-coated extended-release tablet

clues.kinetics: Oral bioavailability is 60% to 87%, and food has no significant effect on absorption. About 45% is bound to plasma protein, and it is cleared mainly by CYP3A metabolism and urinary excretion.
clues.substance: A hydrochloride salt, an odorless crystalline powder with a molecular weight of 315.4 for the active moiety.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA in strengths from 10 mg to 80 mg, dosed every 12 hours.
clues.safety: Boxed warning on addiction, abuse and misuse, and on life-threatening respiratory depression. Contraindicated with known or suspected gastrointestinal obstruction; constipation, nausea and somnolence are common.
clues.indication: Severe, persistent pain that other treatment options cannot adequately manage, in adults and in selected pediatric patients 11 years of age and older.
clues.mechanism: It is a full agonist that is relatively selective for the mu receptor, though it can bind other opioid receptors at higher doses.

tell: Its extended-release tablets give a 4.5-hour elimination half-life, against 3.2 hours for the immediate-release form.
